Messages.Author: Ankha
Messages.Body:
Name: Protect Thine Own
Cardtype: Political Action
Cost: 0 blood
Requires a justicar or Inner Circle member.
Choose a younger Red List vampire with capacity below 6 or a Red List ally. If the acting vampire is a member of the Inner Circle, you can choose a younger Red List vampire instead. If this referendum is successful, this vampire burns X blood to burn that minion, where X is the capacity of the chosen vampire or the cost of the chosen ally.

Thoughts?

Prince of Paris, France

Ratings Coordinator, Rules Director

Messages.Author: Timo
Messages.Body:
It seems really interesting as it gives a very strong boost to red list and trophy (which is needed).

But you have to be carefull.

Other cards with this kind of text comes with a strong draw back :

both Eldest command undeath and veles' Hunt work on prey only, VH is very fragile facing DT (and is limited to a clan without easy acces to ) and ECU has a built in anti-voter captivation.

What you propose has some kind of drawback : you have to play red list or trump-up charge (I guess TUC would be the card of choice in this situation).

But, with a crypt featuring Adana, Lutz, Raphael and Dmitra (which are by themselves very good in PRE/OBF vote deck), you just have to mixx a good combination of TUC, PTO and VC to have a killing machine.

And now, Enkidu (to some extent) and Mata Hari are unplayable

Messages.Author: FrançoisV
Messages.Body: It seems the only way to properly errata a card with such an effect is to load it with conditions and costs to the point it is practically unplayable anyway. So in the end, why bother ?

Agreed. So why not just go:

Protect Thine Own
Political Action
Cost: 1 blood
Requires a justicar or Inner Circle member.
Choose a non-Camarilla Red List vampire with a capacity below 6. If the acting vampire is a member of the Inner Circle, you may choose any non-Camarilla Red List vampire instead. If this referendum is successful, burn that vampire.

Messages.Author: FrançoisV
Messages.Body:
Actually I'd just not bother having it errata'ed and keep it banned. With just an additional Red List condition one could (and will) argue that it's still too easy to pull off. Well, there are already such concerns with an additional Red List condition and a younger clause and a huge cost in blood; really, if that card can be both broken (meaning "too powerful") and broken (meaning "unplayable") there is no way this card can be errated in a satisfying way.

Or maybe with "burn that vampire and the acting vampire". (I'm not really serious, just keep it banned  )
